notes: Method: robots.txt allows ClaudeBot (empty Disallow) so direct HTTP fetch was used throughout (Tier 1), no CDP/Chrome needed. Homepage HTML (curl, desktop UA) was checked directly for holiday keywords -> only hit was a config string 'defaultPageSlug\":\"tara-diwali-page' (a slug for the site's AI shopping-assistant 'Tara' widget, not a product category). Then pulled the full site XML sitemap index and downloaded/decompressed all 7 Category-sitemap-N.xml.gz files (real product-taxonomy URLs, pattern /slug/c-<code>) plus 3 Custom-sitemap and 4 Content-sitemap files for comparison. Isolated the Home department specifically two ways: (1) 702 'home-<brand>' collection URLs under the mbh21* category-code prefix (Home dept brand pages), and (2) the 300 'luxury-home-*' leaf category URLs under the lsh14* prefix, which is the real Home taxonomy: Bath, Bed, Candles & Fragrances, Curtains, Decor/Home Accent, Furniture, Kitchen, Serveware, Storage, Table Linen, Home Furnishing, Home Essentials, Health & Fitness-Home. Grepped all 1002 of these for diwali/christmas/xmas/holi/raksha/valentine/new-year/festive/celebrat/gift/thanksgiving/easter/eid/mother/father: zero genuine holiday-named nodes. The only near-hits were generic year-round subcategories 'candles-fragrances-gift-sets' and 'home-accent-decorative-gifts' (not holiday-specific) and substring false-positives ('steidl' contains 'eid', 'eastern' contains 'easter', 'mother-denim' is the jeans brand MOTHER, 'mothers-maid' is an unrelated beauty sub-brand) -- none are Mother's/Father's Day categories. Confirmed a real category page (luxury-home-decor-furniture-chairs/c-lsh1418102104) is genuinely SSR-rendered and distinct (838KB, title 'Buy Chairs Online | Tata CLiQ Luxury', 'Chairs' appears 207x with structured product data) -- proving the taxonomy scan method actually surfaces real category pages when they exist. The Content-sitemap (CMS/editorial/partner pages, separate from Category-sitemap) DOES contain many Diwali/Christmas/Valentine/Raksha-Bandhan/festive-named URLs, e.g. b-icicifestive2025tnc, hsbcraksha24banktnc, deutschebankdiwali25tnc, b-fragrancesforchristmas, b-60greatrakshabandhangifts, b-theultimateguidetovalentinesdaygifting, b-rakshabandhanstory, valentinedaymenclpfeb2023, 2023valentinesdayhandbagsclpweb -- but per naming and pattern these are bank-partner offer T&C pages, editorial/blog articles, and dated one-off campaign landing pages (CLP), not product-category nodes. Verified directly: fetching a dated CLP URL (valentinedaymenclpfeb2023) and a deliberately nonsense slug (totally-nonsense-slug-xyz123) both return byte-for-byte the same generic 691KB client-rendered homepage shell (same title, same size) -- i.e. these campaign slugs do not resolve to a distinct page with its own product grid/count, unlike the real category pages which are visibly different and richer. This matches the exact discount-campaign/editorial pattern flagged as exclusion criteria. Conclusion: Tata CLiQ Luxury's Home department has no genuine, stable, holiday-branded product-category taxonomy node (no Diwali, Christmas, New Year, Holi, Raksha Bandhan, Valentine's Day, Easter, Eid, Thanksgiving, Mother's Day, or Father's Day PLP with its own URL/product grid/displayed count) as of 2026-09-04. All Diwali/festive/holiday-adjacent Home merchandising exists only as homepage banners, bank-offer T&C pages, and editorial content -- none of which are in scope per the genuine-PLP test. rows left empty accordingly.
